strengths: Good: BLOCKER-1 closed correctly and minimally. r2 §2.3 hardens `pytorch-interop` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:98`) with the same-repo `if:` guard, `permissions: { contents: read }`, and `timeout-minutes: 30`, while preserving `continue-on-error: true`. Verified directly against the live file: today's job has none of those three (confirmed by reading `ci.yml:94-116` — no `if:`, no `permissions:`, no `timeout-minutes`, `continue-on-error: true` present), so the diff described exactly matches what's needed and nothing else changes (env vars / steps untouched, M4.1 mergeability posture intact).

Good: AT-3032's glob-scan design is the right regression-proofing pattern. It enumerates every `self-hosted`-labelled job across all `.github/workflows/*.yml` rather than hardcoding today's 4 files, so a future self-hosted job (e.g. a hypothetical `intel-gpu-experimental` someone adds ad hoc) is caught automatically if it forgets the fork guard / permissions / timeout. This matches the standard 'assert an invariant over an enumerated set, not a fixed list' defensive-test idiom (same principle GitHub's own `actionlint` custom-rule docs recommend for org-wide workflow policy checks). AT-3034 layers the same glob with value-bounds specifically for timeouts, so the two ATs are complementary, not redundant.

Good: BLOCKER-2 closed with a real no-vacuous-pass contract, not just a parser swap. `saphyr` is pinned as a `[dev-dependencies]`-only addition to `axc-driver` (verified: neither `saphyr` nor `yaml-rust2` nor `serde_yaml` currently appear in `Cargo.lock`, so this is a clean net-new addition with no collision), the parse is unconditional (no `#[cfg]` skip), and AT-3033 is a genuine meta-assertion (non-empty parsed doc set + resolved `jobs` key) that makes it structurally impossible for AT-3020/3021/3024/3025/3026/3032 to silently no-op the way the r1 hedge allowed. This directly answers pessimistic r1's BLOCKER-2 finding, which was correct.

Good: the r2 rejection of `serde_yaml` is correct and is itself a correction of my own r1 test_suggestion (I had suggested `serde_yaml` as the dev-dependency without checking its maintenance status). Pessimistic r1 caught that `serde_yaml` is archived/deprecated by its author; r2's §6.3 explicitly rejects it on that basis and pins `saphyr` instead, with `yaml-rust2` documented as an acceptable fallback if `saphyr`'s current maintenance status doesn't hold up at implementation time. That fallback clause is a sensible hedge given I cannot independently confirm saphyr's exact current crates.io maintenance state from here (see concerns below) — the spec doesn't over-commit to a single unverified claim.

Good: all of my r1 rulings are folded verbatim and correctly attributed. §11.1 upgrades ephemeral/JIT + non-root from 'recommend' to 'REQUIRED' with the same rationale I gave (same-repo guard is the sole primary control, no `environment:` layer, no branch protection on `main`); §11.2 keeps environment-approval docs-only for the same 'redundant second gate for already-trusted collaborators' reasoning; §11.3 marks Windows explicitly out-of-scope in §0 rather than leaving it an implicit omission. AT-3029 anchors the ephemeral+non-root wording so this isn't a doc-only promise that can silently rot.

Good: new §1.4 codifies exactly the skip-vs-pending distinction pessimistic r1 asked about in `questions_for_architect` (job-level `if:`-skip inside a triggered workflow reports success; a workflow that never triggers at all — e.g. via an added `paths:` filter — leaves a required check pending forever). It also adds the concrete, actionable guardrail ('never add a `paths:` filter to these workflows') that prevents a future well-intentioned optimization from silently reopening the exact queue-forever failure mode §1.1 exists to avoid. This is a correct and non-obvious GitHub Actions semantic (required-status-check-skip-equals-pass has been GitHub's behavior since the 2022 product change referenced in my r1 review) applied precisely to the milestone's own design.

Good: Mesa honesty rewrite (§5.3, AT-3035) removes the invented-range risk pessimistic flagged. It now states only what's evidenced (25.2.8 known-bad on Lavapipe, NVIDIA unaffected) and explicitly frames the RADV/ANV known-good version as UNKNOWN/TBD rather than fabricating a plausible-sounding version number — the correct epistemic posture for a claim that literally cannot be tested without the hardware this milestone is prep for.

Good: timeouts (30/90/30) are proportionate to the actual work each job does — 30 min for the per-PR GPU-test-suite-plus-bench-gate (no source build), 90 min for the A/B job that source-builds `test-backend-ops` from a pinned llama.cpp checkout (the dominant-cost step correctly identified in §3.1), 30 min for the now-hardened `pytorch-interop`. These bound the single-GPU-box lockup risk pessimistic flagged without being so tight they'd false-fail a legitimate slow build.

Good: the evidence-provenance paragraph in §3 (dispatching `github.actor` + full runner log + embedded `vulkaninfo --summary` device string) is honestly scoped as 'deters and audits, does not cryptographically prove' rather than overclaiming tamper-resistance it doesn't have — appropriately modest given this artifact feeds a real go/no-go RFC decision (`UPSTREAM_PR_PLAN.md §7.5`).
concerns: Non-blocking, flagged per the review brief: I cannot independently confirm from here whether `saphyr` is, as of the current date, the actively-maintained successor to `yaml-rust2` with a healthy release cadence on crates.io (my training-data understanding is that `saphyr` is a next-generation rewrite by the same maintainer group that took over `yaml-rust2`, positioned as the recommended forward path — but I cannot verify current download/maintenance stats live). The spec already mitigates this well by (a) stating the justification is 'on maintenance-status grounds' rather than treating it as settled fact, and (b) explicitly permitting `yaml-rust2` as an equally-acceptable fallback (§6.3: 'Either `saphyr` or `yaml-rust2` is acceptable to the Coder'). Recommend the Coder do a 60-second crates.io/GitHub-freshness check on `saphyr` at add-time (last release date, open-issue trend) before running `cargo add saphyr --dev`, and fall back to `yaml-rust2` without a spec amendment if `saphyr` looks stale — the spec's own wording already permits this, so no revision is needed, just a note for the Coder phase.

Trivial: §12's LOC table doesn't list a line item for the `Cargo.lock` diff (saphyr + its transitive deps will add lockfile lines beyond the '~1 LOC' `Cargo.toml` entry). Immaterial to the ~1,266 estimate or the zero-`src/`-LOC invariant (lockfiles are generated, not authored), just noting for completeness — not a revision request.

Trivial: §6.4's actionlint checksum-pinning describes the mechanism (download pinned release, verify SHA-256 against a committed checksum) but doesn't name the specific version/hash to pin — appropriately left to Coder-time (pinning a checksum in a design doc that predates the Coder phase would itself be a stale-pin risk), and the spec correctly notes actionlint is never load-bearing for the security ATs, so this doesn't gate approval.
validation_against_existing: Direct read of `.github/workflows/ci.yml:94-116` confirms the described pre-r2 state of `pytorch-interop` (no `if:`, no `permissions:`, no `timeout-minutes`, `continue-on-error: true` present) matches §2.3's premise exactly — the hardening diff described is accurate and minimal.

`Cargo.lock` and `crates/axc-driver/Cargo.toml` (dev-dependencies section, read directly) confirm no YAML parser is present today and no name collision exists for `saphyr` — the r2 dependency addition is clean.

Grep across `.md`/`.rs` files for `AT-30(19|2x|3x)` confirms zero collisions with the existing AT-ID space (prior ceiling AT-3018, as I verified in r1); the AT-3032-3035 extension is likewise collision-free.

My own r1 verdict (`EB1prep-optimistic-design-review.json`, prior revision) and pessimistic r1's verdict (`EB1prep-pessimistic-design-review.json`) both re-read for this pass: every CRITICAL, must-fix warning, and open-question ruling from both r1 reviews maps onto a specific, correctly-scoped r2 change (§2.3/§2.4/AT-3032 ↔ BLOCKER-1; §6.3/AT-3033 ↔ BLOCKER-2; §§2.3/3.1/4.1/4.2/AT-3034 ↔ timeouts; §5.3/AT-3035 ↔ Mesa honesty; §1.4/AT-3029 ↔ branch-protection question; §11 ↔ the three open-question rulings; §3 provenance + §3.1 skip_llama_build guard + §6.4 actionlint pin ↔ the three warnings). No r1 finding was dropped or only partially addressed.
test_suggestions: None blocking. Optional, cheap addition for the Coder phase: since `saphyr`'s maintenance status is the one claim in this spec I can't verify live (see concerns), consider having `eb1_workflow_ci.rs`'s doc comment record which parser was actually chosen and why, so a future maintainer auditing the dev-dependency doesn't have to re-derive the r2 rationale from this milestone doc.
summary: r2 correctly closes both r1 CRITICAL blockers with real fixes, not hedges: the live pytorch-interop fork-execution hole is hardened in place with a diff I verified matches the actual current file state, and it's covered by a regression-proof glob-scan AT (AT-3032) rather than a per-file list; the vacuous-security-AT risk is closed by pinning saphyr as a test-only dev-dependency with an unconditional parse and a genuine no-op-detecting meta-assertion (AT-3033), correctly rejecting the deprecated serde_yaml (a correction of my own r1 suggestion, which pessimistic r1 caught and r2 fixed). All three must-fix warnings (timeouts, Mesa-honesty, branch-protection posture) and all three open-question rulings from both r1 reviews are folded in with matching rationale, and I verified the AT range (3019-3035) is collision-free and the saphyr addition has no naming conflict against the live Cargo.lock/Cargo.toml. The only residual concern is non-blocking and flagged per the review brief: I cannot independently confirm saphyr's exact current maintenance status from here, but the spec already hedges this correctly by permitting yaml-rust2 as an equally-acceptable fallback with no required spec amendment. APPROVE.
